frontMatter.introduction:
Mars Stitch Ltd. is a leading manufacturer and exporter of children's and ladies' woven garments, committed to quality, innovation, and sustainability. Established in Tongi, Gazipur, Bangladesh, our company has over 10+ years of industry experience, serving international markets in the USA, Europe, and beyond.

We operate with a strong focus on operational excellence, employee well-being, environmental responsibility, and ethical business practices. Our mission is to create high-quality, sustainable apparel while ensuring compliance with global labor, environmental, and workplace safety standards.
frontMatter.scope:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual applies to all employees, contractors, and stakeholders involved in Mars Stitch Ltd.'s operations.

It serves as a guideline for best practices, compliance measures, and operational processes in various aspects, including:
Workplace Safety & Health Standards
Production & Process Optimization
Environmental & Sustainability Practices
Employee Conduct & Ethical Guidelines
Supply Chain & Vendor Management
Data Security & Confidentiality
Internal Audits & Compliance Monitoring
This SOP Manual must be strictly followed by all employees and is subject to periodic updates based on legal regulations, industry best practices, and company policies.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
To maintain efficiency, compliance, and continuous improvement, this SOP Manual will be reviewed annually by the Compliance & Operations Team in collaboration with the HR, Safety, and Environmental Management Teams.

The review process includes:
1. Annual SOP Review Meeting – To assess effectiveness and identify necessary revisions.
2. Employee & Stakeholder Feedback – Suggestions from employees, auditors, and external stakeholders.
3. Regulatory Compliance Check – Ensuring alignment with Bangladesh labor laws, industry standards, and buyer requirements.
4. Implementation of Changes – Updates communicated through training sessions and official company notifications.

blocks.text: This SOP outlines preventive measures and control actions to ensure a safe, healthy, and secure workplace for all employees at Mars Stitch Ltd. It covers ergonomic safety, hazardous substance exposure, climatic conditions, machine safety, fire prevention, and security force conduct to maintain compliance with Bangladesh labor laws and global workplace safety standards.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and security personnel working at Mars Stitch Ltd. facilities, including production areas, office environments, and outdoor workspaces.

steps.heading: Risk Factors for Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (MSDs)

body.text: Prolonged standing, repetitive movements, poor posture, and improper workstation setup can lead to musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) affecting muscles, tendons, and nerves.

Workstation Ergonomics: Adjustable seating, anti-fatigue mats, and proper desk height.
Task Rotation: Employees performing repetitive motions must rotate tasks every two hours to reduce strain.
Ergonomic Training: Monthly training sessions on proper posture and movement.
Break Schedules: Mandatory 5-minute micro-breaks every hour for employees performing repetitive tasks.
Medical Screening: Periodic health checks for early detection of ergonomic-related symptoms.
Unsecured moving parts, improper use of equipment, and lack of safety training can result in workplace injuries.

Machine Guarding: All hazardous machinery must have protective barriers.
Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) Procedures: Machines must be powered down and locked before maintenance.
Mandatory PPE: Employees operating machinery must wear appropriate protective gear.
Operator Training: Only trained personnel are allowed to operate industrial machines.
Regular Safety Inspections: Equipment must be inspected monthly for defects.

sections.title: Safety Protocols for Handling Hazardous Substances

body.text: Hazardous substances may include chemical solvents, dyes, adhesives, and industrial cleaning agents.

Proper Storage & Labeling: All chemicals must be stored in ventilated, locked cabinets with clear labeling.
PPE Requirements: Employees must wear gloves, masks, goggles, and protective clothing when handling chemicals.
Ventilation Systems: Factory areas with hazardous chemicals must have exhaust fans and air purification units.
Emergency Spill Response: Clearly marked spill kits available in all work areas.
Employee Training: Annual training on chemical handling and safety procedures.

sections.title: Measures for Employee Protection in Extreme Weather Conditions

body.text: Employees working in outdoor environments may be exposed to high temperatures, humidity, and heat stress.

Hydration Stations: Drinking water stations must be available every 50 meters in outdoor work areas.
Protective Clothing: Employees working under direct sunlight must wear light-colored, breathable clothing.
Cooling Breaks: Outdoor workers must be provided with 10-minute cooling breaks every hour.
Heat Stress Monitoring: Supervisors must monitor temperature levels and report heat warnings.
First-Aid Support: Trained personnel must be available to handle heat exhaustion and dehydration cases.

sections.title: Security Conduct & Use of Force Policy

body.text: Security personnel are responsible for protecting company assets and ensuring workplace safety but must operate within legal and ethical guidelines.

Training on Conflict Resolution: Security officers must complete quarterly training on de-escalation tactics.
Clear Use of Force Policy: Security teams are strictly prohibited from using physical force unless in self-defense or legal enforcement situations.
Incident Reporting Protocol: Any use of force must be reported within 24 hours and reviewed by senior management.
Freedom of Movement Protection: Employees must not be unlawfully detained, searched, or restricted from movement.
Regular Security Audits: Compliance teams must conduct monthly assessments on security force conduct.
Flammable materials, electrical faults, and improper storage can lead to fire hazards.

Fire Drills & Evacuation Training: Mandatory quarterly fire drills for all employees.
Fire Extinguisher Availability: Fire extinguishers must be placed every 30 meters in all workspaces.
Smoke & Heat Detectors: Installed in all factory sections for early detection.
Fire Exit Routes: Clearly marked and free from obstruction.
Emergency Response Team (ERT): A designated team responsible for leading evacuations and first-aid response.

blocks.text: Mars Stitch Ltd. will conduct annual audits to ensure compliance with ergonomic safety, hazardous substance controls, climate safety, security regulations, machine safety, and fire prevention measures. Employees are encouraged to report any violations or concerns to the HR & Compliance Department.

This SOP outlines the sustainable energy management and carbon reduction initiatives at Mars Stitch Ltd. The purpose is to enhance energy efficiency, optimize resource utilization, and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across our production, logistics, and office operations. These initiatives align with our commitment to environmental responsibility, regulatory compliance, and long-term sustainability goals.

This SOP applies to all operational units, production facilities, transportation networks, and administrative offices within Mars Stitch Ltd. It covers energy consumption across manufacturing plants, warehouses, logistics, and corporate premises.

body.text:
LED Lighting Optimization: Transitioning to high-efficiency LED lighting across all facilities, reducing electricity usage.
Smart Motor Technology: Implementing Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) motors, which adapt speed dynamically to demand, cutting energy waste.
Automated Power Management: Utilizing smart sensors and automated shutdown protocols to minimize idle energy consumption.
Annual Energy Performance Review: Conducting regular audits to identify and implement further energy-saving innovations.

Industrial Heat Recovery: Installing waste heat recovery units to capture excess thermal energy for reuse in production processes.
Exhaust Heat Reutilization: Diverting heat from machinery and generators to power secondary operations.
Integrated CHP Solutions: Deploying Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems that generate both electricity and thermal energy, enhancing efficiency.
Steam & Hot Water Recycling: Reusing waste steam from textile processing to reduce energy reliance.

Natural Gas Implementation: Replacing coal and diesel with clean-burning natural gas to lower emissions.
Onsite Solar Power Generation: Installing solar panels across factory rooftops to harness renewable energy.
Biomass & Alternative Fuels: Exploring bio-waste energy utilization to reduce fossil fuel dependency.
Real-Time Energy Monitoring: Deploying fuel tracking systems to ensure energy optimization and emission reduction.
Workforce Training on Green Energy: Conducting training programs to promote energy-saving behaviors among employees.

Fleet Electrification & Hybrid Adoption: Transitioning to electric and hybrid vehicles for logistics operations.
Employee Carpool & Shuttle System: Encouraging ride-sharing, company buses, and public transit incentives.
Alternative Fuel Adoption: Implementing biofuel and compressed natural gas (CNG) solutions for transport.
Eco-Driving Certification: Training drivers on fuel-efficient driving techniques to cut emissions.

sections.title: Energy Optimization in Office & Facility Operations

body.text:
Green IT & Energy-Saving Electronics: Implementing power-saving settings on all workstations.
Smart Energy Management: Utilizing motion-sensor lighting to eliminate energy waste.
Sustainable Procurement Strategies: Acquiring eco-friendly office equipment and supplies.
Employee Sustainability Engagement: Hosting workshops and awareness sessions on energy conservation.

blocks.text: Mars Stitch Ltd. will conduct annual sustainability audits and carbon impact assessments to ensure compliance with environmental standards. Employees are encouraged to report any energy-related concerns to the Sustainability & Compliance Division.

This SOP outlines Mars Stitch Ltd.'s commitment to efficient water management, minimizing water consumption, and implementing sustainable practices in production and facility operations. It aims to reduce environmental impact through technological advancements and operational improvements.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and stakeholders at Mars Stitch Ltd., including manufacturing units, office spaces, and other operational facilities where water usage is a key factor.

substeps.text: Mars Stitch Ltd. employs advanced water recycling technologies to reclaim and reuse water in various operational processes, such as production cooling, irrigation, and cleaning.
All reclaimed water undergoes necessary treatment before reuse, ensuring compliance with environmental standards.
IoT-based water sensors have been implemented to monitor and optimize water usage in real time.
The company utilizes closed-loop water systems to reduce overall water consumption.
Counter current washing techniques are adopted to maximize efficiency in fabric processing.
Automated tracking systems measure water savings and efficiency improvements per unit of fabric processed.
Mars Stitch Ltd. integrates water-efficient dyeing machines that minimize water consumption per fabric unit.
Heat recovery systems in dyeing processes help reduce the need for excessive water heating.
Waterless dyeing technology is being tested for large-scale implementation to further reduce water dependency.
The company is gradually transitioning to air dye technology and supercritical CO2 dyeing, which eliminate water usage in fabric dyeing.
Staff is trained to optimize dye use and prevent unnecessary water wastage.

steps.heading: Efficient Water Use in Industrial Cleaning

substeps.text: The company has installed water-efficient washers and flow control systems to minimize water usage in garment cleaning.
Regular process optimization is carried out to reduce water dependency in washing operations.
Smart water meters are used to track and regulate water usage per production cycle.

steps.heading: Reuse of Process Water for Cleaning

substeps.text: Wastewater from washing units is treated and reused for non-critical cleaning processes.
Pre-rinsing and optimized detergent application ensure minimum water use while maintaining quality standards.
Employee training includes water-efficient cleaning techniques to minimize waste.
Mars Stitch Ltd. has implemented a rainwater harvesting system across all production units to collect and store rainwater for operational use.
Collected rainwater is used for cooling systems, irrigation, and general facility cleaning.
Rainwater harvesting contributes to reducing dependency on groundwater sources.
Rainwater undergoes filtration to remove contaminants before being directed to utility applications.
The system reduces dependence on municipal water supplies and mitigates groundwater depletion.
All rainwater harvesting processes adhere to environmental regulations set by the Bangladesh Environmental Conservation Act (BECA).
The company conducts annual water risk assessments to evaluate potential shortages, contamination risks, and usage inefficiencies.
Risk mitigation plans are formulated based on assessment outcomes.
Independent third-party audits are conducted to validate assessment results.
Wastewater discharge is monitored to ensure compliance with environmental regulations.
Treatment plants are regularly maintained to uphold water quality and sustainability goals.
The company aims for zero liquid discharge by improving wastewater recycling efficiency.

blocks.text:
8.1 Water Conservation Training Programs

All employees undergo periodic training on sustainable water management practices.

Best practices in water conservation, waste reduction, and process optimization are shared through workshops and digital learning platforms.

Training includes modules on emergency response procedures for water contamination incidents.

8.2 Incentives for Water-Saving Initiatives

Employees contributing to water-saving innovations are recognized through an internal reward program.

Departments achieving significant water savings are provided additional resources for continuous improvements.

A suggestion program is in place for employees to propose water-saving solutions.

Mars Stitch Ltd. commits to maintaining industry best practices in water conservation. This SOP will be reviewed annually to incorporate the latest sustainable water management techniques and regulatory changes. The Environmental & Compliance Department is responsible for overseeing the implementation and tracking of all water conservation measures.

The objective is to develop products that require fewer resources, generate less waste, and contribute to circular economy initiatives.

This procedure applies to all product design, development, and production teams at Mars Stitch Ltd., including supply chain partners involved in raw material selection, product testing, and distribution.

steps.heading: 3.1 Best Practices for Efficient Product Use & Maintenance

substeps.text: Provide clear instructions on reducing resource consumption during product use, including energy, water, and chemical efficiency.
Implement training programs for consumers and retailers on proper product handling to maximize durability.
Develop easy-to-understand care labels for all products, outlining optimal washing, drying, and storage techniques.

steps.heading: 3.2 Proper Storage & Handling of Chemical-Based Products

substeps.text: Ensure safe storage guidelines for chemical-based products to prevent leaks, emissions, and hazardous exposure.
Provide step-by-step guides on chemical application to minimize environmental impact and reduce waste.
Offer refillable packaging options to encourage responsible consumption.
Develop garments that require less water, energy, and chemical inputs during their use phase.
Utilize advanced dyeing and finishing techniques that reduce chemical dependency.
Integrate energy-efficient components into production machinery to decrease electricity and water demand.
Prioritize eco-friendly and biodegradable materials to lessen the environmental footprint.
Enhance durability through fiber strengthening techniques to reduce premature product disposal.
Utilize digital prototyping to optimize fabric consumption and minimize production waste.

steps.heading: 5. Innovations for Microfiber Shedding & Wear Reduction

substeps.text: Apply advanced finishing treatments to fabrics that reduce shedding during washing.

Enhance fabric tensile strength by incorporating reinforced stitching techniques.
Provide after-sales repair and maintenance services to encourage long-term product use.
Introduce take-back programs where consumers can return worn products for refurbishment or recycling.
Transition to biodegradable, recyclable, or reusable packaging for all products.

This SOP outlines the standardized process for evaluating both employee and buyer performance at Mars Stitch Ltd. It ensures systematic assessment, continuous improvement, and alignment with organizational goals.

This SOP applies to all employees and buyers associated with Mars Stitch Ltd. The process ensures fair, objective, and consistent evaluation to enhance productivity, maintain quality standards, and foster business relationships.
The purpose of the employee performance evaluation is to assess individual contributions, identify areas for improvement, and establish a structured approach for professional growth.

narrative.text: Employees will be evaluated based on the following key performance indicators (KPIs):

Job Knowledge & Skills
Work Quality & Accuracy
Productivity & Efficiency
Communication & Teamwork
Initiative & Problem-Solving
Adherence to Company Policies
Punctuality & Attendance

body.text: Evaluations will be conducted annually (Year-End).
The evaluation process includes self-assessment, supervisor review, and 360-degree feedback from peers and subordinates where applicable.
Employees will participate in one-on-one discussions with their supervisors to receive feedback and set performance goals.
Employees are rated on a 5-point scale (Excellent, Good, Satisfactory, Needs Improvement, Unsatisfactory).
Employees with a rating of "Needs Improvement" or below will be placed under a structured PIP to address deficiencies.

blocks.text:
All performance evaluation records are maintained by the HR Department.
The Employee Performance Evaluation Form must be completed and signed by both the employee and the supervisor.
The buyer performance evaluation ensures that our business partners meet our quality, compliance, and delivery standards, fostering long-term collaborations.

narrative.text: Buyers will be assessed based on the following key metrics:

Order Accuracy & Quality Compliance
Timely Payments
Business Relationship & Communication
Ethical Sourcing & Compliance
Sustainability Practices
Overall Satisfaction Level

body.text: Evaluations will be conducted annually.
Data will be gathered through order tracking systems, supplier feedback, and compliance audits.
Buyers will be categorized based on a scoring matrix as Preferred, Acceptable, or Under Review.
If a buyer is rated as Under Review, corrective measures will be implemented, including warning notices or reconsideration of business agreements.

blocks.text:
All buyer evaluation forms are maintained by the Procurement & Compliance Departments.
The Buyer Performance Evaluation Form must be reviewed and signed by the Procurement Manager.

The HR and Procurement teams are responsible for ensuring adherence to this SOP.
This SOP will be reviewed annually to incorporate process improvements.

This SOP establishes clear guidelines and approval procedures for sensitive transactions such as gifts, travel, entertainment, and other expenses that involve external stakeholders. The aim is to ensure transparency, compliance with ethical standards, and prevent conflicts of interest within Mars Stitch Ltd.

This procedure applies to all employees, management, and stakeholders involved in financial transactions, business dealings, or any engagement that includes gifts, sponsored travel, entertainment, hospitality, or donations.

rows.definition: Any monetary or non-monetary gift, item, or favor received from or offered to external stakeholders.
Business-related travel funded by external parties.
Invitations to corporate events, dinners, or recreational activities provided by business partners.
Contributions made to individuals, organizations, or charities on behalf of the company.

blocks.text: Sensitive transactions refer to business-related activities that may be perceived as influencing decision-making or compromising ethical integrity. These include:

substeps.text: Employees must not accept or offer gifts exceeding BDT 5,000 without prior approval.
Gifts above this threshold require approval from the Department Head and Compliance Officer.
Employees must declare all received gifts in the Gift Declaration Form (GDF-01) within 5 working days.
Promotional items of nominal value (e.g., calendars, pens) are exempt from approval.
Travel expenses sponsored by vendors, suppliers, or third parties must be pre-approved by the HR & Compliance Department.
Employees must submit a Travel Approval Request (TAR-02) at least 10 working days before the trip.
All travel-related reimbursements must include valid receipts and an Expense Report (ER-03).
Employees must obtain written approval before attending any externally sponsored entertainment event.
Invitations from suppliers, customers, or third parties must be declared using the Event Approval Form (EAF-04).
Any entertainment exceeding BDT 15,000 per event requires CEO approval.
Employees are prohibited from making donations or sponsorship commitments on behalf of the company without authorization.
Requests must be submitted via the Sponsorship & Donation Request Form (SDR-05) for review by the Corporate Affairs Department.

blocks.text:
All transactions must be documented and retained for at least 3 years.
The Finance & Compliance Team will conduct quarterly audits to ensure compliance with this SOP.
Non-compliance may result in disciplinary action in accordance with company policy.

narrative.text:
Any suspected violations must be reported via the Whistleblower Hotline or emailed to compliance@marsstitch.com.
Reports will be kept confidential, and no retaliatory action will be taken against whistleblowers.

blocks.text: This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Compliance Department to align with regulatory changes and company policies.

sops.title: Incident Response to Confidential Information Breaches

blocks.text: This SOP establishes a structured incident response procedure for detecting, containing, investigating, and mitigating breaches of confidential information at Mars Stitch Ltd. The objective is to minimize risk, protect company assets, ensure business continuity, and maintain compliance with relevant regulations.

This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, third-party vendors, and any other personnel with access to Mars Stitch Ltd.'s confidential information, whether stored electronically or physically. It covers breaches affecting:

Employee Data (personal records, payroll details, performance reports)
Customer & Vendor Information (contracts, invoices, payment details)
Financial & Business Documents (budget reports, trade secrets, intellectual property)
IT Systems & Digital Assets (company databases, cloud storage, internal communication channels)
Sensitive Operational Data (supply chain, production schedules, compliance reports)
Any Other Proprietary or Classified Information essential to Mars Stitch Ltd.’s operations

sections.title: Definition of a Confidential Information Breach

blocks.text: A confidential information breach is defined as unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or destruction of sensitive company data, resulting in potential security risks. Examples include:

Cybersecurity Incidents: Hacking, malware attacks, phishing scams, or ransomware attacks compromising confidential data.
Unauthorized Access: Internal or external personnel accessing sensitive information without proper clearance.
Physical Document Exposure: Loss or theft of printed reports, contracts, or confidential files.
Device Theft or Loss: Company laptops, USB drives, or mobile devices containing sensitive data being lost or stolen.
Improper Disposal: Insecure disposal of confidential paper documents or electronic files, leading to data exposure.

sections.title: Incident Response Procedure (IRP) for Confidential Information Breaches

body.text:
Employees must report suspected data breaches immediately to the IT Security Team via:
Email: security@marsstitch.com
Phone: +880-1827-753341
The IT team will monitor system logs, intrusion alerts, and suspicious activities to verify the breach.
If a breach is confirmed, the Incident Response Team (IRT) will be activated to assess the situation.

The IT Security Team will isolate compromised systems to prevent further unauthorized access.
If the breach involves third-party vendors, their access will be temporarily revoked until a full review is completed.
In cases of device theft/loss, remote locking and data-wiping mechanisms will be activated.
Legal and compliance teams will determine regulatory notification requirements for affected individuals.

The Cybersecurity & Compliance Team will conduct a root cause analysis to determine the origin and extent of the breach.
The financial, operational, and reputational impact will be assessed.
Employees involved in handling the compromised data will be interviewed for further insights.

The Compliance Department will notify affected parties (employees, customers, vendors) within 72 hours, in line with legal requirements.
Law enforcement agencies and regulatory bodies will be informed, if necessary.
Affected employees will receive guidance on security precautions to prevent future incidents.

The IT Team will apply necessary security patches, update firewall settings, and reset compromised credentials.
Affected systems will be restored from secure backups to ensure minimal disruption to business operations.
All recovery actions will be documented in the Incident Report Form (IRF-07) for audit and compliance purposes.

A post-mortem analysis will be conducted to identify vulnerabilities and areas for improvement.
Employees involved in the incident will undergo additional security training to reinforce best practices.
The Incident Response Plan (IRP) will be updated with lessons learned and mitigation strategies.

narrative.text:
All security incidents must be logged in the Confidential Information Breach Register (CIBR-08).
Reports must include:
Date and time of the incident
Nature of the breach
Affected systems and data
Actions taken
Preventive measures recommended
Records will be retained for five years for legal and compliance review.

blocks.text:
Employees responsible for negligence or misconduct leading to a data breach will face disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
Compliance audits will be conducted quarterly to ensure all security protocols are followed.

This SOP will be reviewed annually by the IT Security & Compliance Department.
Updates will be made based on evolving security threats, regulatory changes, and industry best practices.

This SOP establishes guidelines for the secure retention, access control, and stakeholder consent related to confidential information at Mars Stitch Ltd. The objective is to protect third-party data, ensure regulatory compliance, and promote transparent data management practices.
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers handling sensitive company and client data, including but not limited to:

Customer & Vendor Information (contracts, invoices, payment records)
Employee Records (personal details, performance reviews, payroll data)
Financial & Operational Documents (budget reports, supply chain records, regulatory filings)
Confidential Business Data (trade secrets, intellectual property, business strategies)
Digital & Physical Records stored in company systems or archives

3.1 Establishing Retention Periods for Data

Mars Stitch Ltd. follows a Records Retention Schedule (RRS) specifying the required retention period for various data types based on legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

The schedule includes the following categories:

Financial Records: Retained for 7 years (audit and tax compliance)
Employee Records: Retained for 5 years post-employment
Customer & Vendor Data: Retained for 5 years after the last transaction
Legal Contracts: Retained for as long as the contract is valid + 5 years
Confidential Business Documents: Retention period determined by management based on relevance

3.2 Secure Disposal of Expired Records

Physical Documents: Must be shredded before disposal to prevent unauthorized retrieval.

Digital Records: Must be permanently deleted from all storage locations, including backup servers.

A Destruction Log must be maintained for tracking disposal actions.

body.text:
4.1 Access Control Measures

Access to third-party confidential data is restricted based on job roles and responsibilities.

Only authorized personnel (determined by department heads) can access sensitive records.

Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is enforced for systems containing sensitive data.

Data Encryption: All confidential digital files must be encrypted using AES-256 encryption standards.

Physical Security Measures:

Confidential files stored in locked cabinets with limited access.
Surveillance cameras monitor physical storage areas.
Biometric authentication for server rooms and secure storage areas.

4.2 Monitoring & Audit of Access Logs

All access to sensitive information is logged and monitored using company IT systems.

The IT Security Team conducts quarterly audits to detect unauthorized access attempts.

Employees accessing high-risk data must receive security clearance from senior management.

steps.heading: Obtaining Stakeholder Consent for Data Collection & Processing

body.text:
5.1 Obtaining Stakeholder Consent for Data Collection & Processing

Mars Stitch Ltd. follows a Transparent Data Collection Policy that requires obtaining explicit consent from stakeholders before gathering personal or business data.

Stakeholders must be informed about:

Purpose of data collection (e.g., contract fulfillment, compliance, marketing)
Types of data collected (name, contact details, financial records, etc.)
Duration of retention as per the company’s Records Retention Schedule
Third-party sharing policies, if applicable

5.2 Data Processing & Sharing Guidelines

Customer & Vendor Agreements must include a Data Privacy Clause outlining:

How data will be processed, stored, and protected
Who has access to their data
How they can request modification or deletion of their data

Before sharing data with external service providers, a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) must be signed, ensuring compliance with privacy laws.

Customers must be given an opt-out option for non-essential data processing activities (e.g., marketing communications).

blocks.text:
6.1 Incident Reporting & Response Plan

Any suspected unauthorized access, data leak, or breach must be reported immediately to the IT Security Team at:

Email: security@marsstitch.com
Phone: +880-1827-753341
The Incident Response Team (IRT) will:

Investigate the breach
Contain the security threat
Notify affected stakeholders within 72 hours
Implement remedial actions to prevent future incidents

6.2 Compliance with Data Protection Regulations

Mars Stitch Ltd. ensures compliance with Bangladesh Data Protection Laws and international standards, including:

ISO 27001 (Information Security Management)
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) for clients in the EU
Local labor and commercial data retention policies

7.1 Data Protection Training

All employees handling sensitive data must complete mandatory data security training every 6 months.

Training includes:

Best practices for handling confidential data
Recognizing phishing and cybersecurity threats
Proper disposal of sensitive records

7.2 Reporting Violations & Non-Compliance

Employees suspecting unauthorized data handling can report it to the Compliance Officer at:

Email: compliance@marsstitch.com
Confidential Hotline: +880-1827-753341
Reports will be investigated under the Whistleblower Protection Policy, ensuring confidentiality and non-retaliation.

This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Data Security & Compliance Department.
Changes will be made based on technological advancements, regulatory updates, and internal audit findings.
The purpose of this SOP is to establish a structured and standardized process for conducting internal audits and due diligence assessments at Mars Stitch Ltd. It aims to:

Ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and company policies.
Identify and mitigate risks associated with third-party relationships, financial transactions, and corruption.
Improve operational transparency and accountability.
Strengthen internal controls to uphold ethical business practices.

This SOP applies to all internal departments, employees, vendors, suppliers, contractors, and any third parties involved in the business operations of Mars Stitch Ltd. The audit process will be applicable to:

Procurement & Vendor Selection
Supply Chain Transparency
Compliance with Anti-Corruption & Anti-Bribery Laws
Employee Awareness of Ethical Conduct
Financial Transactions & Sensitive Approvals
Occupational Health & Safety Compliance
Data Protection & Information Security

body.text:
Internal audits will be conducted semi-annually or as required based on risk assessments.
The Compliance & Internal Audit Team will determine the audit scope, objectives, and criteria.
A detailed Audit Plan will be developed, outlining departments, processes, and third-party relationships to be reviewed.

The audit team will collect relevant documentation, including policies, reports, financial records, and employee statements.
Random and targeted site inspections will be conducted, particularly for high-risk areas such as procurement, financial transactions, and third-party engagements.
Employees and stakeholders will be interviewed to assess compliance with ethical and operational standards.
Data analytics tools may be used to review financial transactions and detect anomalies.
A detailed audit report will be prepared, outlining:

Areas reviewed
Findings and observations
Non-compliance issues
Risk level assessments (low, medium, high)
Recommendations for corrective actions
Audit reports will be reviewed and signed by the Head of Compliance before being shared with management.

Identified issues will be assigned to responsible departments with clear action plans and deadlines.
The Compliance Team will follow up within 30 days to ensure corrective measures have been implemented.
Persistent non-compliance may result in disciplinary actions or process overhauls.

All vendors, suppliers, and business partners must undergo a risk-based due diligence assessment before engagement. High-risk vendors will be subjected to enhanced scrutiny, including background checks, financial reviews, and compliance history analysis.

Business legitimacy verification (registration documents, tax compliance).
Past involvement in corruption, fraud, or legal violations.
Compliance with Mars Stitch Ltd.’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption policies.
Ethical labor practices, human rights adherence, and sustainability policies.

All third-party relationships will be periodically reassessed.
Any red flags, complaints, or discrepancies will trigger an immediate review and possible termination of contracts.

blocks.text:
All audit reports, vendor due diligence documents, risk assessments, and corrective action plans will be securely stored for a minimum of five years.
Access to audit records will be restricted to authorized personnel only.

This SOP will be reviewed annually by the Compliance Team and revised as needed to align with evolving regulatory requirements and business risks.
Lessons learned from past audits will be incorporated into future risk mitigation strategies.
